scope: Broaden open-source DWG/DXF peer comparison to writer omission, section/block ownership, entity-sequence syntax, control-character framing, and strict-versus-recovery validation; refine the implementation plan without promoting support claims.

method.kind: Primary Autodesk DXF references, upstream LibreDWG and ACadSharp issue reports, ezdxf official documentation, and local source/test cross-check
method.sourcePinning: GitHub issue pages are mutable reports. Status and reproducer notes are scoped to their recorded authors/dates. No peer commit or executable was run.
method.evidenceRule: Peer issues are failure-mode/test leads, not proof of a matching libdxfrw defect. A peer fix, self-read, aggregate entity count, or recovery-mode parse does not establish full feature semantics or clean output.

evidence.observed: The issue author reports an AC1032 named block with eight owned HATCH/LWPOLYLINE entities emitted empty. A second contributor reports reproduction over 43 real AC1032 files, skipped paper-space bodies, the analogous defect in ASCII and binary writers, and a cheap BLOCK_RECORD versus BLOCK body-count invariant. The report says the bug remained on LibreDWG master at the contributor's September 9, 2026 observation.
doesNotEstablish: the issue has been independently reproduced in this review
all supported block/layout records must always be non-empty
whole-file entity-count equality proves owner or handle closure
evidence.planUse: Add owner-aware block/layout output manifests and missing source-authored consecutive-block/layout controls only where existing targets do not already cover them; validate ASCII and binary routes separately.

evidence.topic: Broken child reference versus end-of-list and sequence framing
evidence.observed: LibreDWG #1357 reported that an unresolved child reference was conflated with end-of-list, and the reporter later verified a master fix against three AC1021 inputs. #1351 reported INSERT code 66=1 without ATTRIB/SEQEND; the reporter later verified a master fix. Autodesk's INSERT/SEQEND references specify that the nonzero attributes-follow flag requires ATTRIB records terminated by SEQEND.
doesNotEstablish: either historical LibreDWG issue is still present on current master
continuing after a failed child is always semantically safe without a loss diagnostic
a syntactically closed sequence preserved all source attributes
evidence.planUse: Keep list termination distinct from unresolved child status; preserve later valid siblings where policy permits and report the skipped source identity. Require structurally valid ATTRIB/SEQEND output or atomic refusal.

evidence.topic: Zero-valued fields, attribute tags, and embedded MTEXT
evidence.observed: The issue reports a DXF-to-DWG route rejecting HATCH group 21 when the valid Y coordinate is exactly zero, dropping unusual producer-authored ATTDEF/ATTRIB tags, and mishandling embedded-MTEXT fields. The report's proposed patch labels the embedded-field handling a stopgap and the issue remained open at review time.
doesNotEstablish: all unusual attribute tags are valid in every target release
that a lossy skip is equivalent to typed preservation
evidence.localCrossCheck: tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp already includes runtime-authored ASCII/binary explicit-zero HATCH and embedded ATTRIB/ATTDEF controls. These do not establish every DXF-to-DWG/DWG-to-DXF version route or native acceptance.
evidence.planUse: Reuse existing generated controls, add only a focused counterpart when changing an uncovered route, and use ODA/Autodesk field rules for presence-versus-zero and profile validity.

evidence.topic: Physical DXF string framing and control characters
evidence.observed: LibreDWG #1408 reports literal CR inside complex TEXT/MTEXT values producing an empty physical line at a DXF group-code position and a strict ezdxf parse failure; the reporter says the exact complex case was not reduced to a source-authored minimal sample. Autodesk documents that DXF record values are physical group-code/value pairs, making record-boundary corruption distinct from decoded-text equality.
doesNotEstablish: the exact peer reproducer is minimal or independently reproduced here
which escaping behavior is correct without the applicable text/profile specification
evidence.planUse: Add tiny generated CR/LF/CRLF ASCII and binary controls with a following group and record sentinel; assert physical framing and either spec-backed escaping or pre-publication refusal. Do not copy the peer drawing.

evidence.topic: Strict readback, record-level tolerance, and recovery-mode limits
evidence.observed: ACadSharp #1184 reports a file-provided out-of-range plot value causing whole LAYOUT objects to be discarded or a read to fail. ezdxf documents normal read separately from recovery; recovery may ignore binary XRECORD data, can be lossy on save, and audits can repair/fix fields while retaining unrecoverable errors.
doesNotEstablish: that clamping is correct for any particular DXF/DWG field
that a recovery-mode load is a clean output-validation pass
evidence.planUse: Keep errors local to a record when the authoritative format contract permits, emit diagnostics, and do not invent values. At composed qualification, strict parser plus recorded audit findings is the acceptance route; recovery is diagnostic-only.

observed: The current opt-in writer ledger records primary handle plus normalized record type and section and rejects duplicate emitted handles at finalization.
HATCH finalization queries expected emitted type and ENTITIES/BLOCKS section.
Existing generated tests cover ASCII/binary HATCH explicit-zero input, embedded ATTRIB/ATTDEF data, block ownership, sequence boundaries, and writer-ledger identity/duplicates.

The ledger does not yet establish a universal source/output identity crosswalk, per-owner emitted inventory, all-route candidate completeness, FIELD graph edge compatibility, or independent parse-back parity.

prioritize: physical DXF framing and INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND validity
per-block/per-layout emitted child and owner completeness
unresolved-child continuation with explicit loss diagnostics
one pinned strict independent parser/audit at the composed checkpoint
